transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-05
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya H (Redwood AE), Liam O (Redwood SE), Priya N (Redwood SE), Daniel P (CTO, QuantumWorks), Renee O (Head of Security), Samira K (Infra), Oliver W (PM)

Summary:
- POC scoping for a 3-month Dedicated pilot focused on secure on-prem / VPC-delivered inference for QuantumWorks' document summarization product.
- Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, quality acceptance), workload sizing, benchmark plan, timelines, and security/compliance requirements (SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS).
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to send compliance artifacts and benchmark template; QuantumWorks to provide sample prompts and traffic profile; follow-up sizing deep dive to be scheduled.

Topics covered: Success criteria; Pilot workload shape and sizing; Benchmark definitions and measurement; Security controls and certification; Network and operational constraints; Timeline and commercial ask.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya H: Alright hello everyone, thanks for carving time. We'll run through scope for the POC and make sure we capture must-haves, especially on the security side.
[00:18] Daniel Park: Yep, thanks. Quick note — Renee is here from security, Samira from infra, and Oliver who owns the product. We're looking to be pretty strict on controls for this pilot; we want to validate both performance and that nothing leaks.
[00:32] Renee Ortiz: hi everyone, um, two things upfront: SOC two coverage is a hard requirement and we need audit logs that show per-request metadata. Also we use SAML SSO with SCIM for provisioning.
[00:48] Liam O'Connor: makes sense — on our side we can provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestations, and our platform supports SAML and SCIM; we'll share the SSO metadata file. A question: do you want RBAC down to the model-route level or team-level?
[01:05] Renee Ortiz: team-level is minimal, but we prefer route-level for production. For the pilot team-level is ok as long as we have per-token audit logs retained for 90 days.
[01:22] Priya Nair: just to clarify, when you say audit logs you mean request metadata, response size, model id, user id, and whether the KV cache was hit, correct?
[01:31] Renee Ortiz: yes, exactly. And we need logs to be immutable and exportable to our SIEM (we use Splunk).
[01:40] Maya H: great — that's doable. We'll include export instructions and our recommended retention policies.
[01:46] Oliver White: on the success criteria side, product wants p99 latency for short prompts to be under 250ms and median under 80ms; quality acceptance is 92% pass on our manual eval set. Does that sound feasible?
[02:02] Liam O'Connor: p99 250ms is tight depending on your model and whether you run private or hosted. For Dedicated with optimized kernels and quantization we can usually hit under 200ms on A100-ish hardware for 512-token context for some models, but it depends on the model family and sequence length.
[02:20] Samira Khan: background on infra — we plan to run this in a VPC initially, but we have a potential air-gapped test later. For the pilot we need a clear network egress list and port requirements; also KMS integration for key wrapping is a must.
[02:38] Maya H: we'll provide the VPC connectivity doc and an egress IP list. For KMS we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS/HSM) and envelope encryption, we'll include that in the architecture note.
[02:50] Daniel Park: traffic shape — what numbers should we expect to size for? Right now production target is ~40 requests per second average with spikes up to 120 rps. But for the pilot we want to test at realistic load: say 50 rps sustained for 1 hour and a burst test to 150 rps. Token distribution average 80 tokens per request, 99th percentile 600 tokens.
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: that's helpful. For benchmarking we'll run steady-state throughput tests and spike tests. We'll also use prefix caching and batching knobs to represent your expected workload.
[03:25] Priya Nair: can you confirm token accounting? 80 tokens average translates to about X tokens per second at 50 rps — roughly 4k tokens/sec sustained. We'll include cost/run estimates in the sizing doc.
[03:38] Oliver White: quality measurement — we will provide 250 canonical prompts with expected outputs and a pass/fail rubric; acceptance threshold is 92% pass across the set.
[03:49] Liam O'Connor: good, we'll run automated comparisons and also sample human review to validate model drift and hallucination rates.
[03:58] Renee Ortiz: compliance questions: do you provide a private control plane for the Dedicated pilot? We need to ensure config changes are auditable and only reachable via SAML-authenticated accounts.
[04:10] Maya H: yes, for Dedicated and Private deployments we offer a private control plane option with SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Changes to rollout policies and model versions create audit entries and we can forward them to Splunk.
[04:23] Daniel Park: on data residency — some customer content must remain in EU. Our pilot corpus is US-only, but by the time we scale we may require region pinning.
[04:33] Priya Nair: note captured — we support regional pinning for model serving and storage. We'll document how to pin to EU regions later.
[04:42] Liam O'Connor: benchmark plan: we propose three phases — baseline functional tests (latency/throughput/ops), correctness/quality evaluation against your 250-prompt set, and soak/stability test for 6 hours at pilot load. Acceptance criteria: p99 latency <250ms (short prompts), throughput within 10% of desired RPS, and quality pass >=92%.
[05:05] Samira Khan: do you run the benchmarks in our VPC or your hosted environment? Network latency will skew p99.
[05:13] Liam O'Connor: we can run both: an initial hosted-run to validate the pipeline and then run in your VPC/Dedicated environment to measure realistic p99 including network. For the VPC run we'll need a small staging cluster that matches your planned Dedicated shape.
[05:27] Oliver White: timeline — we want to start the pilot by mid-February and run three months. Is that realistic?
[05:33] Maya H: it's tight but doable if we get artifacts quickly. Timeline proposed: week of Feb 9 — kick-off + sign pilot SOW; Feb 10–16 — infra provisioning and SSO setup; Feb 17–23 — baseline benchmarks + initial quality run; Feb 24 — decision point to continue full pilot.
[05:50] Daniel Park: okay, good to have checkpoints.
[05:54] Renee Ortiz: a couple of more security items — do you support hardware-backed key storage or HSM integration? We need to ensure model embeddings are encrypted at rest.
[06:06] Maya H: yes, HSM-backed KMS is supported; we also have configurable envelope encryption for model artifacts and logs.
[06:12] Priya Nair: on RBAC, we can set role binding to restrict model deploy permissions to certain groups; we also log the actor id and JWT claims in audit trails.
[06:22] Samira Khan: what about data deletion? For the pilot we need a guaranteed scrub of transient request logs and any cache keys after 30 days.
[06:32] Maya H: we can set retention windows and provide a deletion runbook; for pilot we can set 30-day retention for request content and 90 days for operational logs unless you request shorter.
[06:43] Liam O'Connor: small caveat on caching — prefix and KV cache are used to reduce cost and latency. If you require strict ephemeral behavior we can disable caching for certain routes for the pilot, but that increases cost.
[06:58] Daniel Park: that's fine — for test routes we can disable caching, but for regular workloads we want cache on. We'll document which routes are sensitive.
[07:08] Oliver White: procurement note — we'll need a one-page compliance checklist for legal; please include SOC 2 Type II scope and ISO statement.
[07:16] Maya H: we'll attach the checklist with the SOC/ISO artifacts.
[07:20] Renee Ortiz: also need proof of vulnerability scanning cadence and patch management policy for the Managed infra.
[07:28] Priya Nair: we'll include our published patching and vulnerability remediation SLAs in the security packet.
[07:34] Liam O'Connor: back to benchmarks — can you share a sample of the 250 prompts now or do you need internal sign-off first?
[07:42] Daniel Park: I can share a redacted set with Samira and Oliver by Friday. Some prompts include PII so we'll redact.
[07:50] Samira Khan: for the VPC run, we'll need a small test instance with two GPU nodes to start, and access for Redwood engineers via a jump host.
[07:58] Priya Nair: noted — we'll put together a runbook for jump host and least-priv access.
[08:04] Liam O'Connor: success criteria recap: 1) p99 < 250ms for short prompts; 2) throughput within 10% of requested RPS (50 sustained, burst 150); 3) quality pass >=92% on your eval set; 4) security controls in place: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, SAML/SCIM SSO, RBAC, exportable audit logs to Splunk, KMS/HSM integration, 30-day deletion for request content.
[08:30] Oliver White: yep that covers it. A question: what's the expected duration for Redwood to run full benchmarks once we hand over the eval set?
[08:37] Liam O'Connor: once we get the prompts and a traffic shape file, we can run hosted baselines in 48 hours and a VPC/Dedicated run typically takes 3–5 business days including coordination.
[08:47] Daniel Park: procurement timeline: we need SOW draft, pricing for pilot and a handshake on escalation channels for issues.
[08:54] Maya H: pricing will be provided as a simple line item for Dedicated reserve plus usage overage and a professional services estimate for the on-site setup. We'll include incident response contacts for escalation.
[09:05] Renee Ortiz: last compliance note — we may request a small security questionnaire (SIG or similar). Will you fill that?
[09:12] Maya H: yes, we'll fill the SIG or complete your vendor questionnaire; expect that with the SOC/ISO artifacts.
[09:18] Samira Khan: follow-up technical — do you support pinning models to older versions for rollback? We want canary control.
[09:25] Priya Nair: yes, rollouts support canary and automatic rollback policies; we log version changes and provide a snapshot of performance metrics per rollout.
[09:33] Oliver White: OK let's close with agreed next steps and responsibilities.
[09:38] Maya H: recap: Maya sends compliance packet and network diagram; Liam shares benchmark template and example scripts; QuantumWorks provides 250-prompt eval set and traffic profile; Priya schedules deep-dive sizing with Samira. We'll target a Feb 9 kickoff if legal and procurement can turn SOW quickly.
[09:58] Daniel Park: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[10:02] Maya H: thanks — we'll follow up in email and shoot for that Feb 9 date.
